questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical understanding of OS caches, concurrency, and read-ahead/write-back interplay. It probes how to design a small, real subsystem with correctness under contention.

## Key Concepts
- Fixed-size cache with hash + LRU
- Concurrency: in_flight dedup and waiting
- Read-ahead and write-back eviction
- Correctness under concurrent reads/writes

## Code Example
```pseudo
block_read(id):
  if cache.has(id): return cache.get(id)
  if in_flight.contains(id): wait
  in_flight.add(id)
  data = disk_read(id)
  cache.insert(id, data)
  in_flight.remove(id)
  return data

evict_block():
  b = cache.LRU_clean()
  if b.dirty: write_back(b)
  cache.remove(b)
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of synchronized lazy paging, cross-process visibility, and NUMA-aware fairness in a realistic kernel path.

## Key Concepts
- Per-page state machine (idle/in-flight/ready)
- CAS-based owner election to avoid duplicative work

- NUMA affinity and cross-core contention

```c
  atomic_int state; // 0 idle, 1 in-flight, 2 ready
  // ... other fields
} page_t;
```

- How would you extend this to support prefetch hints and read-ahead when multiple faults occur?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design scalable, NUMA-aware caches with cross-node synchronization, eviction policies, and prefetch heuristics under real workloads.

## Key Concepts
- NUMA locality, per-node memory pools, cross-node credits
- CAS-based page claim, zero/fault paths, async IO
- Adaptive prefetch/read-ahead and fairness under contention
